transcript: A Republican senator has suggested that the photograph of MitchMcConnell published as Proof of Life that he's fine.Might be fake.And this senator says he heard it from a source.Now, as we've talked about a lot in the last two weeks, Mitch McConnell'shealth has gotten more and more attention, especially over the last few days afterhe was in the hospital for 28 days, with no public statementas to why he was there.People wanted to know, is he alive?Is he on life support? Is he unconscious?And on Sunday, a photograph was releasedshowing Mitch McConnell sitting next to his wife, Elaine Chao.We already looked at the picture and kind of went througha lot of the reasons that some people are questioningwhether the picture is real or whether it is new.And then Senator Ron Johnson was asked about it, and instead of saying,I don't know enough about it to comment, Johnson says,I actually have a source that says the picture is an older picture.Maybe it's not a new picture, and there is a lot wrapped up in this.So let's first listen to Ron Johnson.Then we will sort of break down each of the claims he makes the election.Now, Mitch McConnell, can we talk a little Mitch McConnell through?Because I saw a picture that I'm not sure I believe is actually Mitch McConnellfrom the hospital.After what I've heard and what I've seen, do you believeMitch McConnell is the one who said, I'm okay?Here's the picture of my wife, Elaine Chao, and I in that hospital bed.But Ijust heard from some some of the source that was an older photo.So I really don't know. I haven't talked to Mitch.I certainly wish he and his family well.I hope he can recover.Listen, it's sad to watch people age, no matter who that person is.You know, I've served with Mr. McConnell for 16 years.Okay.Obviously disagree with himon a host of things, but I also know he loves this country.He loves he loves the Senate.He reviews the Senate.And so again, I do try and put the best construction on things.I try and look for the best in people.Mitch McConnell also loves this country, so I wish him well.I hope he recovers.I hope he can come back and and contribute to and vote with the president's agenda.All right.So people keep referring to a 2023 Getty image.And what a lot of people are pointing out is, hey, look, Mitch McConnell is wearingthe exact same red checkered shirt in the Getty image from 2023.So the picture that was released of Mitch McConnellmust actually be from 2023.Now, there are a couple of problems with that claim.Number one, Mitch McConnell is clearly wearing different glassesin the picture released on Sunday than he is in this 2023 picture.And people do wear the same shirts twice.That's he might have just worn that red checkered shirt more than once.If anything, it arguably proves the hospital photo is realbecause it is a shirtthat Mitch McConnell has been independently documented to own.Now, there is another aspect to this,and this is what I think is the most important aspect.They never really said the picture was taken on Sunday.It was certainly implied.It was certainly insinuated.It was called a proof of life picture along with a statement. Butthat photograph may not have been taken on Sunday and it may be an old picture.And families don't always releasehospital pictures when they are talking about someone in the hospital.They might release a picture from when Mitch looked better.If indeed Mitch McConnell isn't doing well but is recovering, let's just imaginefor a second they might say, listen, he doesn't look great.He is recovering, but he doesn't look great.Let's put out an older picture now. Is it dishonest?I think to some degreeit isbecause if you're acting asking for proof of life,you want to see the state of Mitch McConnell right now.And the family might have said, we're not putting outa picture of what he looks like right now, because we don't want to know.They could also be putting out an old picture because he's deador because he's unconscious, or we just don't know.But the the checking and the picture, he wore the same shirt 2023.I don't know that that really proves anything.Now, what caught my attention wasn't the shirt so much,it was how quickly the conversation moved from here's a photograph tomaybe the whole thing is fake.And this is a habit that we've seen develop over the years.For a very long time, many Republican leaders have encouragedsupporters to constantly believe they were being misled.The media is lying to you.The Justice Department is lying to you.The FBI is lying to you.Scientists are lying to you. Doctors are lying to you.Teachers, your kids, teachers are definitely lying to you.Election officials are lying to you.And that mindset has become automatic for a lot of these folks.And so you get a new piece of information.And the first reaction is immediately, I'm now suspicious.And then they look for evidence that confirms or reaffirms their suspicion.And that's what Senator Ron Johnson's comments really illustrate, whether hegenuinely thought this is an old picture or was repeating something he heard.It's not really the important part.The important part is I heard from a source and that's enough.That's enough to publicly cast doubt on the health statusof one of his own colleagues.And the irony to me is that once you teach millions of peoplethat deception is everywhere, that instinct is not going tostay confined only to Democrats or to journalists orthe government agencies that you don't like.Eventually that's going to get turned inward.And so now a Republican senators picture is very suspicious.And a Republican senators medical condition requiresa lot of speculation to figure out what's going on.And even information coming from your own side ends up getting filteredthrough the assumption that someone must be hiding something here.Now, I do think healthy skepticism is valuable.I am not completely convinced that Mitch McConnell is fine.I'm not. I'm not completely convinced of that.And we shouldn't just blindly accept everything that were handed.But skepticism works by asking for evidence, and suspicion worksby assuming there's some hidden real story until and unless proven otherwise.And these are admittedly very different ways of looking at the world.AI is going to make this way harder, way harder to detect.I have a whole the whole final section of my new book, Pay Attention, is abouthow AI is going to affect the creator space and the news media and politicalreporting and elections. Deepfakes are real.Image manipulation is now as easy as just typing into ChatGPT what you want,and so public officialsshould be careful before accepting digital media at face value.But they also should be careful before suggestingthat something that might be authentic is actually fake.Because when you can dismiss every picture as AI and every video is AI,it becomes really difficult for society to agree on even the most basic facts.So Ron Johnson just made a comment that was like 30s long,but it really gives us a glimpse into this political culture of suspicionas the default.And that is a habit that, listen, they've lost control of the monsterthat they built.If this topic is interesting, please do preorder my book.Pay attention.You can get one of the limited numberof signed copies remaining at David Parkman attention.That also has links to all the other ways to get the book.And if you want this particular book, this is not a green screen, by the way.Look.Whoops, the book fell.If you want.Here's the book.If you want this specific copy,submit your preorder receipt to info at David Parkmanand we'll put you in a raffle for this particular book.Thanks for watching.Check out another one of our videos and make sure to subscribe!So YouTube keeps our content in your feed,and if you prefer audio, subscribe to the podcast on Spotify or Apple.
